situation.person: Nigerian mother around 2 months postpartum with shaky supply who added formula in the first 12 weeks, judged by breast-is-best relatives and just-give-formula friends
situation.specific_situation: She nurses when she can and tops up when she must, but hides the tins and lies at the market because both camps shame her. Every feed is negotiated under surveillance, so feeding never settles into a routine and she cannot ask for help openly.
situation.trigger: Late or low milk with weight loss, then a nurse said top up with formula.
situation.problem: No defensible combo routine exists, therefore every bottle restarts the argument and the shame.
situation.failed_attempt: Tried exclusive breastfeeding, pap with tiger-nut and oats, and prayer, and nothing changed in two weeks except bloating.
situation.emotional_stake: Wants to be a good mother, not a failed one; the shame feels heavier than the baby.
situation.desired_transformation: She can nurse when she can and top up when she needs, and can say it out loud without flinching; the combo plan is posted and followed.

NHS mixed-feeding guidance: introducing formula affects breast-milk production; maintain supply by expressing regularly; use slow-flow teats; cut down gradually to minimise mastitis risk.
WHO home formula preparation: reconstitute with water no cooler than 70 C; discard unfinished bottles; refrigerate promptly; sterilise all equipment.
evidence.source: WHO safe preparation and storage of powdered infant formula guideline

evidence.claim: UNICEF UK: any breastfeeding is valuable; where supplementation occurs, use the minimum consistent with safety and plan return to full breastfeeding; mothers who combine remain breastfeeding mothers.
evidence.source: UNICEF UK Baby Friendly maximising-breastmilk standards (2022-02-11)

evidence.claim: Paced-bottle technique is consensus practice with preliminary-only outcome evidence; it must never be presented as proven to preserve breastfeeding.
UK formula-stigma survey figures describe UK mothers who used formula and must never be restated as Nigerian combo-feeding prevalence.
evidence.source: Authoring Wave 1 evidence review (Fallon et al. 2016 scope containment)

safety.scope_boundary: This transformation coordinates FEED C. Shame-free combo feeding - breast plus formula without hiding only. It does not diagnose, treat, or replace professional care, and it does not cover adjacent situations outside its recorded nucleus.
escalation_rules: Route per the verified shared crisis/escalation list (RED = emergency now, AMBER = urgent today, GREEN = supported this week) - safety-standard 3; no numbers are invented here
